cur:objects-coin-nikephoros-ii-basil-ii-.summary: The obverse shows the bust of Christ Pantokrator in a cross-nimbus, blessing and holding a jewelled Gospel book; on the reverse the soldier-emperor Nikephoros II Phokas and the young Basil II, the legitimate heir, hold a patriarchal cross between them. Under Nikephoros the full-weight gold coin acquired its later name, histamenon. Christ's image sanctions the partnership between the victorious general and the Macedonian dynasty.
facts: Wikipedia notes that Nikephoros II introduced a lighter gold coin, the tetarteron, after which the traditional full-weight solidus came to be called the histamenon ('standard' coin).
